Own-domain press total ≈ 9.12. (2) Press% percentile-rank to signed `=C3/MAX($C$3:$C$535)` (mirror CMTEFIX). Result: Marshall #193 to #473 (Press% -0.07), Welch #188 to #374, AOC #184 to #344. Leg pillar: raw/max was TRIED on leg (J,P) 2026-07-01 and REVERTED: leg-stance raw is long-tailed (allies +17..+27), so value/MAX squashed the mid-board and floated disengaged skeptics UP (AOC #344 to #191, Welch to #279); back on PERCENTRANK. Leg-stance stays "muted" (AOC leg raw -2.58 gives Leg% 0.102 positive) but fine: the press fix already ranks opponents low (final: AOC #344 / Welch #374 / Marshall #473). A winsorized normalizer (÷ 90th-pct magnitude, not max) would make leg bite without compression if ever wanted. Durable code: `apply_press_dedup.py`, `apply_raw_max_norm.py`, `apply_committee_fix.py` (CMTEFIX), `apply_leg_stance.py`. See `cu-signflip-directionality` / `press-classification-user-domain`.

s10.old: Key discoveries this pass: (a) the Sub Layer to Legislative reference is **off-by-one for all 533** (Sub has 3 header rows, Legislative has 2, so same row number = next member; Byron read Carlos Gimenez), BUT "fixing" it alone made the board WRONG because (b) **legislative co-sponsorship is directionless VOLUME** (rewards prolific members like Durbin regardless of stance) and (c) **press is the only directional signal** (signed -1..+1, enemies negative) yet was wired at ~0.05 vs legislative ~1.0; (d) **committee data was incomplete** (Tim Scott=Banking CHAIR read 0); (e) **1,066 `#REF!`** in Legislative-Raw cols DG/DO = dead **external-workbook links `[1]!Table1`** (data lost, zeroed); (f) **Aaron Bean #1 phantom** = 5 entirely-empty Legislative cols (CDFI×3, Payments-CoSpon, FoM-CoSpon) produced a spurious 1.0 for the first data row via empty-column min-max.

s10.old: The fix = **score restructured into 4 buckets, each min-max normalized then weighted by EDITABLE cells at `Rank & Allocation!S2:S5`: Press 0.40 / Legislative 0.20 / Committee 0.35 / Demographic 0.05** (user first said 40/40/15/5 but 40% legislative floats Durbin, so moved excess to committee). **Legislative is PRESS-GATED** at first (col D = leg_volume × sign(press_lean); anti-CU activity counts negative). Composites are written as VALUES (cols C/D/E/F); normalize/score/RANK/allocation + Coalition Profiles aggregates are LIVE formulas. Allocation now distributes the FULL $2M (score-proportional among top 133, no cap). **Committee data collected fresh from Wikipedia 119th-Congress rosters** (House Financial Services, Senate Banking, House+Senate Small Business; chairs/vice/ranking/subcommittee chairs) to a new **`Committee Data`** sheet; rubric = membership (Banking/FS=3, SmallBiz=1.5) + leadership (Chair+6, RM+4, ViceChair+3, SubChair+2.5, Financial-Institutions sub+4, SubRM+1.5), composite = 0.4·membership+0.6·leadership (later replaced by the reverse-engineered (Membership+Leadership)/2 scoring above). **REFINED (same session, later): press-gating was REMOVED** (see superseded). Bias audit also found: **chamber bias** (Senators avg rank 196 vs House 283, more press/broader committees), **missing-data floor** (51 members with no press AND no committee sink to ~#355 regardless of stance; the very bottom is now no-signal members like Richard Hudson/Roger Wicker, not enemies), mild **Democratic demographic tilt** (demo bucket D 0.52 vs R 0.34, at 5% weight), and committee is the single strongest score driver (corr 0.89, defensible = objective position). NOTE user's correction: **Warren & Waters ARE CU-supportive** (anti-big-bank aligns with CUs); do NOT push them down; their high committee-leader rank is correct. **FINAL board then: Tim Scott #1, French Hill #2, Roger Williams #3, Andy Barr #6, Britt #16, Steil #20, Lummis #27; enemies Durbin #490, Marshall #524, Welch #505, Gooden #523, Lofgren #326. Zero errors, $2M/133.** Remaining SOURCE-DATA (not model) gaps: see Known Issues. COM recalc tip (June guidance): force-killing a headless Excel orphan can trigger autorecover that silently rolls back the openpyxl write; verify the header/values persisted on disk after recalc; prefer try/finally cleanup over `Stop-Process`. **OneDrive race confirmed:** the file lives in OneDrive\Desktop, so an openpyxl-save immediately followed by a COM Open can race OneDrive sync and the COM crash reverts the file to a pre-write version. FIX that worked: do the openpyxl write, verify it persisted by re-reading with openpyxl (NOT COM), then **recalc on a LOCAL copy outside OneDrive** (`Copy-Item $src $env:TEMP\mb_work.xlsx; COM recalc temp; Copy-Item temp $src`). Also: independently compute the board in Python (composites to min-max to 0.40/0.20/0.35/0.05 to rank) as the source-of-truth verification rather than relying on COM-cached values.
